title: Localization of normalized integral left coefficient laws
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness of the schemes is imposed. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories $C_s(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ [def-sf-categories], completed at integral stages and with positive finite levels $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\ge1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ use the completed integral category $C_{E,\mathrm{int}}(T)$ and its raw scalar localization $C_E(T)$, whose objects are integral objects and whose Hom groups are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{int}}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, with localization functor $R_E^T$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Fix a compactification $c$ of $f$. Give integral functors $F_{E,\mathrm{int}}$ and rational functors $F_E$, and the actual completed integral and rational scalar extensions $T_{L/E,\mathrm{int}}^T,T_{L/E}^T$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use the scalar associators $\alpha$ and unitors $u$ normalized by balanced tensor multiplication; their rational versions are the localized integral maps under the canonical ordinary/completed scalar identifications. Allow all $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embeddings by identifying each source field with its image.

Suppose integral comparisons $q^{\mathrm{int}}_{L/E}$ satisfy the left scalar composition and identity equations for these integral associators and unitors. Suppose given rational comparisons $q_{L/E}:T_{L/E}^YF_E\cong F_LT_{L/E}^X$ whose components on each integral representative are the localized integral components, with the specified scalar object identifications. Require the following normalization on all rational morphisms, in addition to the object equalities $F_E(R_E^XK)=R_E^Y(F_{E,\mathrm{int}}K)$:
$$F_E\!\left(\sum_\nu a_\nu R_E^X(h_\nu)\right)=\sum_\nu a_\nu R_E^Y(F_{E,\mathrm{int}}(h_\nu)),\quad a_\nu\in E.$$
Here $h_\nu$ are integral arrows with the indicated common endpoints.

Then every rational input has an integral representative in the uniform finite-Tor domain, and for every $E\to L\to M$ and $K\in C_E(X)$ one has
$$F_M(\alpha_{X,K})q_{M/L,T_{L/E}^XK}T_{M/L}^Y(q_{L/E,K})=q_{M/E,K}\alpha_{Y,F_EK},\qquad F_E(u_{X,K})q_{E/E,K}=u_{Y,F_EK}.$$
In particular the functor-image terms $F_M(\alpha_{X,K})$ and $F_E(u_{X,K})$ are the localized integral functor-image terms under the same identifications. This conclusion concerns the given rational functors on arrows, and does not assert that localization reflects equality.

proof.text: Let $K\in C_E(X)$. Raw localization has exactly the integral objects, so write $K=R_E^X\widetilde K$ with $\widetilde K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Since $\ell\ne p$, $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. The residue-Tor lemma gives $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$; thus this very representative has one Tor interval for all positive reductions. This proves the domain assertion without replacing the raw category by an idempotent completion.

source.place: Derived inverse limits, rationalization, common-stage construction and refinement-compatible adjunction; extracted normalized coefficient argument, old steps 5

proof.text: Suppress the given scalar object identifications and write $R_F=R_F^Y$ on target arrows. The raw scalar formula gives $T_{M/L}^Y(R_L h)=R_M(T_{M/L,\mathrm{int}}^Yh)$ for every integral arrow $h$. The assumed morphism normalization, specialized to the singleton sum with coefficient $1$, gives $F_M(R_M^Xh)=R_M(F_{M,\mathrm{int}}h)$. In particular, since $\alpha_{X,K}=R_M^X(\alpha^{\mathrm{int}}_{X,\widetilde K})$ and $u_{X,K}=R_E^X(u^{\mathrm{int}}_{X,\widetilde K})$ by hypothesis, their images under the given rational functors are $R_M(F_{M,\mathrm{int}}(\alpha^{\mathrm{int}}_{X,\widetilde K}))$ and $R_E(F_{E,\mathrm{int}}(u^{\mathrm{int}}_{X,\widetilde K}))$. These equalities use the normalization on arrows, beyond the object equalities. In Lean the component specifications of sfRationalScalarComp and sfRationalScalarUnit from lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition give the precise heterogeneous equalities, and specializing sfRationalHomCoordinates to h tensor 1 identifies the singleton normalization with the localization map.

source.place: Derived inverse limits, rationalization, common-stage construction and refinement-compatible adjunction; extracted normalized coefficient argument, old steps 5

proof.text:
Apply $R_M$ to the assumed integral composition equation at $\widetilde K$. Its composition rule $(h\otimes1)(g\otimes1)=(hg)\otimes1$ gives
$$R_M(F_{M,\mathrm{int}}(\alpha_X^{\mathrm{int}}))\,R_M(q^{\mathrm{int}}_{M/L,T_{L/E,\mathrm{int}}^X\widetilde K})\,R_M(T_{M/L,\mathrm{int}}^Y(q^{\mathrm{int}}_{L/E,\widetilde K}))=R_M(q^{\mathrm{int}}_{M/E,\widetilde K})\,R_M(\alpha_Y^{\mathrm{int}}).$$
The middle $q$ component is evaluated on the integral object $T_{L/E,\mathrm{int}}^X\widetilde K$, which represents $T_{L/E}^XK$. Substitute Step 2 and the stipulated localized components of $q$ and $\alpha_Y$. The displayed equality becomes exactly $F_M(\alpha_{X,K})q_{M/L,T_{L/E}^XK}T_{M/L}^Y(q_{L/E,K})=q_{M/E,K}\alpha_{Y,F_EK}$.

source.place: Derived inverse limits, rationalization, common-stage construction and refinement-compatible adjunction; extracted normalized coefficient argument, old steps 5

proof.text:
Likewise apply $R_E$ to the integral identity equation:
$$R_E(F_{E,\mathrm{int}}(u^{\mathrm{int}}_{X,\widetilde K}))\,R_E(q^{\mathrm{int}}_{E/E,\widetilde K})=R_E(u^{\mathrm{int}}_{Y,F_{E,\mathrm{int}}\widetilde K}).$$
The same composition rule and Step 2 identify this with $F_E(u_{X,K})q_{E/E,K}=u_{Y,F_EK}$. Step 1 covers every rational object. For an embedding rather than a literal inclusion, identify each field with its specified image, as allowed in the hypotheses; the same formulas then apply. Both arguments apply localization to a known equality and need no injectivity of integral Hom maps.
